items.reply: This is as specified: --shout goes before the name (spec and the settled design question both say so), so `greet.sh ada --shout` printing `hello ada` is the intended behaviour. Other flag positions are out of scope for this MR.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:6 takes any argument as the name; with sh as dash/macOS sh, `sh bin/greet.sh 'a\tb\c'` now prints a tab and drops the newline, where the previous version printed the name verbatim.
finding.claim: `echo` interprets backslash escapes under POSIX sh, so a name containing `\` is altered even without --shout, breaking 'without --shout nothing changes'.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:6 accepts any name; `sh bin/greet.sh --shout josé` prints `HELLO JOSé`. Nothing in the code or spec limits names to ASCII.
finding.claim: `tr a-z A-Z` upper-cases only ASCII letters, so non-ASCII names come out half-capitalised under --shout.
finding.suggestion: Use `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'`, which follows the locale where tr supports it (macOS tr does; GNU tr remains byte-based).

items.reply: Checked: `sh bin/greet.sh --shout` prints `HELLO WORLD`. The shift on line 5 empties $1, so line 6 falls back to world, and line 8 capitalises it.
The commit message reads `Add --shout`; we see no typo there, and the thread is already resolved.
